calibration.method: k (level) and mu (directivity) minimise the squared differences of these four levels, rendered in free field for the 00 buck load; c_T makes its positive phase the published 456 microseconds. Three numbers fitted to five published ones. The published guns have 18 and 18.5 in barrels, this one 20 in: the model has almost no barrel-length term, so the difference is ignored

a_duration.note: c_T is set from this figure, so agreement is by construction; the independent check is the spectrum below

negative_phase.note: fixed by the Friedlander form: no published negative-phase figure for a 12 gauge was found

spectrum.position: 1 m left of the shooter at ear height, 42.67 ms window
spectrum.note: the paper also says the maximum band exceeded 130 dB for most weapons. The model does not reach that: its whole level over the window is about 133 dB, and Maher and Shaw's energy figure scaled to this microphone gives about 131 dB, so no single band of an impulse can hold 130 dB. Not reconciled

b_duration.note: open ground must be under the published outdoor figure; the covered firing point must sit between open ground and the indoor values; the room, at the shooter, must fall inside the published indoor range, 30 to 185 ms. Nothing in the room was adjusted to make it so. The published microphones were at instructor positions in rooms whose size is not given

directivity.note: about 15 dB in the text; 145 on axis against a lowest value of 129 gives 16

blowdown.note: no published jet-noise level for a shotgun was found: unvalidated

click_measures.note: how much of the shot is over within 2 ms, and how long each octave band takes to stay 20 dB under its own maximum (2 ms rms envelope). Buckshot at the shooter's ear. Version 1 is in bands_v1.json
